core.title: Map each artifact name to its contract file path with the fixed formula
core.given: An artifact name (first segment, optional intermediate segments, final segment; shape and separators per the profile's contract-name key) is mapped to a contract file path, in any document, code or tooling.
core.when: You write, reference or compute the contract file path for that artifact.
core.then: Derive the path deterministically by the fixed formula: turn each name segment except the last into a directory under the contract root, and the last segment into the filename carrying the contract file suffix.
prefer: Split the artifact name on its separators and turn every part except the last into a directory under the contract root; the last part becomes the filename with the contract file suffix.
avoid: Hand-picked or flattened paths that do not mirror every name segment (e.g. collapsing segments into one filename).
Keeping the artifact name's separator characters in the file path, or using a suffix other than the profile's contract file suffix.
Renaming an artifact without moving the referenced contract path to match.
core.why: The artifact-name -> file-path transform is deterministic, so any tool or reader can locate a contract from its name alone; a path that diverges breaks that lookup.
evidence: For each artifact name, applying the formula yields exactly the referenced or computed contract file path.
verification: Check: for every artifact name paired with a contract file path in any document, code or tooling, recompute the path with the fixed transform (name shape, contract root and contract file suffix come from the profile) and require an exact match; the transform works for any number of intermediate name segments, including zero.
Out of scope: text or code that never maps an artifact name to a contract file path, and files that are neither contract files nor derived from an artifact name.
The rule's glossary term for the deterministic artifact-name -> contract-file-path transform is a realization detail; the transform itself is stated in then and here.

values: contract file (identified by the profile's contract root and contract file suffix)
any file kind (the mapping may be written or referenced in any document, code or tooling)
artifact name mapped to a contract file path
contract file path added, moved or referenced for an artifact

fires: An artifact whose name has only a first and a final segment is mapped to its contract file.
An artifact whose name has several intermediate segments is mapped to its contract file.
A plan artifact, acceptance document or other document references the contract file of a named artifact.
Code, a script or tooling computes or hard-codes the contract file path for an artifact name.
A contract file is added or moved under the contract root for an artifact.
An artifact name is renamed and its contract file path must follow.
doesNotFire: Text or code that never maps an artifact name to a contract file path (e.g. pure behavioral acceptance prose).
Files that are not contract files and are not derived from an artifact name.

neutralityNotes: The core states the mapping parametrically: each name segment except the last becomes a directory under the contract root, the last becomes the filename with the contract file suffix. Every concrete part (name separators ':' and '.', contract root 'contracts/', suffix '.schema.json') reaches the core through three proposed profile keys, because the closed vocabulary has no key for a named contract artifact (urn params), its tree (layout) or its file kind (suffix). The Bun activation fact kind path_glob is outside the core fact vocabulary and is re-expressed as file_kind. Concrete test vectors (evidence[1], verifier_detail[1]), the worked example inside then, and the glossary term id file_mapping stay bunOnly; bun.json remains the worked reference example, so instantiation with the Bun profile values plus these items imposes exactly the Bun obligation.
